title: Canonical coefficient realization respects the ordinary derived direct-image compositor
statement: Let A be any finite commutative ring and f:X→Y, g:Y→Z arbitrary scheme maps. Write RX, RY, RZ for the specified fixed-scalar-to-intrinsic derived equivalences, Gf and Gg for intrinsic derived direct image, Ff and Fg for fixed-scalar derived direct image, and δh:RX⋙Gh≅Fh⋙RY for the section/K-injective-normalized direct-image comparison of [def-sp-finite-intrinsic-direct-adjunction]. Let α:Gf⋙Gg≅G(f≫g) be the adjunction conjugate of the exact intrinsic pullback compositor of [def-sp-finite-intrinsic-open-square], and β:Ff⋙Fg≅F(f≫g) the adjunction conjugate of the fixed-scalar left-derived pullback compositor, using the specified derived adjunctions. For every fixed-scalar derived object J on X, Gg(δf,J);δg,Ff(J);RZ(βJ)=αRX(J);δ(f≫g),J. No coefficient system, operation datum, constructibility, properness or open immersion occurs.

source.place: Coefficient-presentation normalization in step 2 of lem-sf-system-finite-compositor-coordinates; Stacks 00YV, 03D3, 07A5 and 07A6.

proof.text: Transport the ordinary fixed-scalar adjunction through the module equivalences. By definition sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction uses exactly sfIntrinsicDirectImageComparison as its right comparison. Expand sfIntrinsicPullbackComp: it inserts the middle equivalence unit. Naturality and the two triangle identities show that the mate of this pullback compositor is the pasted right comparisons and fixed-scalar compositor. Its scalar action is fixed because all three right comparisons agree on scalar-unit sections.

Choose a K-injective complex representing J. Exact inverse image implies that its right adjoint preserves K-injectives; coefficient equivalences preserve them too. In the K-injective composition normalization use the identity resolution of the first image. The normalization equations for sfIntrinsicDerivedDirectImageComparison identify the three derived comparisons with the localized ordinary comparisons on this representative. The derived Hom bijection takes the ordinary mate equation to the derived mate equation; exact localization of the left adjoints gives sfIntrinsicDerivedPullbackComp, and leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory identifies the fixed left-derived model.

Cancel the middle equivalence unit and counit. This gives the displayed equation on the representative. Naturality transports it along a representative isomorphism to arbitrary J. The zero ring, empty schemes, zero objects and identity maps require no exception.

theorem sfIntrinsicDirectCompositorCoordinates
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (J : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X)
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)))) :
    let B := ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)
    let af := (sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction f A).mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction
    let ag := (sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction g A).mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction
    let adjt := (sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction
      (f ≫ g) A).mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction
    (proEtaleConstantDerivedDirectImage g A).map
        ((sfIntrinsicDerivedDirectImageComparison f A).hom.app J) ≫
      (sfIntrinsicDerivedDirectImageComparison g A).hom.app
        ((lowerStar B f).rightDerivedFunctor.obj J) ≫
      (sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence Z A).functor.map
        ((conjugateIsoEquiv
          ((derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction B g).comp
            (derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction B f))
          (derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction B (f ≫ g))
          (leftDerivedUpperStarComp B f g)).hom.app J) =
    (conjugateIsoEquiv (ag.comp af) adjt
      (sfIntrinsicDerivedPullbackComp A f g)).hom.app
        ((sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence X A).functor.obj J) ≫
      (sfIntrinsicDerivedDirectImageComparison (f ≫ g) A).hom.app J
